So cD2 survives the self-test because the D2-broken world ALSO loses D3 (the record filtering drops LOG and round-68 wholesale, taking JUNK and even D1's redundancy with it). The D2 world is not a single-defect world: it breaks D2 AND D3 simultaneously. A counter that misses D2 alone is invisible to it as long as it still catches (the co-broken) D3. That's a genuine self-test blind spot: the "D2 receipt path absent" world is confounded — it doesn't isolate D2. My real-world X2 mutant (isolated) proves the live counter catches D2; but the self-test could not detect a counter that loses ONLY D2 detection... wait — actually cD2 neutered D2 and the self-test stayed green — exactly that demonstration.

Check: `python3 -I .ufo/waves/round-43/w1/ScrQualityCriteria/check78.py --receipt <round>/receipts/ctl-c1.txt --claim <the cited line>` — it recomputes rows, anchors, controls and the `M`/`D`/`K` classes from `^ok  <NAME>` lines, compares the receipt's `controls=` header and its `0 of <n>` verdict denominator against those counts, and compares each number the claim repeats; a `TALLY_MISMATCH claim M=37 receipt=38` line and `CHECK78: verdict=FAIL` are violations.
